intro.title: useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFetch` to fetch data from an API and manage the loading and error states. You will learn how to encapsulate data-fetching logic into a reusable hook using React's built-in hooks like `useState` and `useEffect`. The main technologies involved are React for building the UI, JavaScript for the logic, and the Fetch API for making HTTP requests. By the end, you'll understand how to simplify data fetching in your components and handle common states like loading and errors efficiently.
intro.usecase: The useFetch pattern is essential in modern web applications where dynamic data loading is required. You'll see this in dashboard interfaces that display real-time metrics, e-commerce product listings with filters, and social media feeds that load new content as users scroll. Developers implement useFetch to handle API calls for user profiles, search results, or inventory data while managing loading states and errors gracefully. This pattern keeps UI components clean by separating data-fetching logic from presentation, making code more maintainable and testable.
